title: Audit a Pallas kernel and its target evidence
hardware: CPU interpretation/simulation available; real TPU runner requires separately validated TPU hardware

stages.title: Grid and precision contract
stages.evidence: Independent full-array checks, singleton/tail fixtures, block ownership and rejected input contracts
stages.expected: PASS stage 1: actual grid semantics, full and partial tiles, singleton rows, two dtypes and rejected contracts
stages.diagnosis: If the last row or column fails, check ceiling division, padding and crop boundaries before changing arithmetic.

stages.title: Fused target-oriented kernel
stages.evidence: Bias-axis and activation-boundary checks, two precisions and an explicit no-fallback target guard
stages.expected: PASS stage 2: fused broadcast contract, ReLU boundaries, tails, two precisions and no CPU target fallback
stages.diagnosis: If interpretation passes but target lowering fails, preserve the target error; interpretation is not a target compilation test.

stages.title: Pipeline semantics and measurement protocol
stages.evidence: Synchronous/buffered comparisons, two/three input buffers, representative shapes and guarded target benchmark; target receipts remain separate
stages.expected: PASS stage 3: actual pipeline CPU simulation, synchronous/buffered agreement, input buffering, tails/dtypes and guarded target benchmark
stages.diagnosis: If buffering changes values, inspect copies and ownership. If hardware is unavailable, keep performance unverified rather than timing simulation.

rubric: Verify every output against an independent represented-input oracle across tails and dtypes
Explain grid coordinates, input windows and unique output ownership
Preserve an explicit float32 compute and final output-cast policy
Execute actual synchronous and buffered Pallas pipeline semantics
Reject unsupported shape, dtype, buffer and target-mode contracts
Separate CPU simulation metadata from actual target backend evidence
Use a guarded TPU-only runner with synchronized warm measurements and a strong JAX baseline
Relate profiling and partitioning decisions to the end-to-end optimization opportunity
setupNote: CPU stages use requirements-cpu.txt with actual Pallas interpretation and TPU-memory simulation. Run from the extracted top folder. The separate target_tpu.py command requires a configured real TPU environment and refuses CPU fallback; no TPU qualification is implied by CPU stage passes.
